Consider the following pairs:
1. IMF—Kristalina Georgieva—Bulgaria
2. World Bank—Ajay Banga—United States
3. UNCTAD—Rebeca Grynspan—Costa Rica
4. ILO—Gilbert F. Houngbo—Togo
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
9.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Georgieva is Bulgarian, Banga is an Indian-born U.S. national, Grynspan is from Costa Rica and Houngbo is from Togo.
9.tq: Check both the office-holder and nationality; a single swapped nationality invalidates a pair.

9.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
9.x: Gilbert F. Houngbo is from Togo, not Ghana. The other three institutional leadership-nationality pairs are correctly matched.
9.tq: Find the one wrong nationality in an otherwise familiar set of institutional pairs.

9.s: The headquarters of Greenpeace is located at:
9.x: Greenpeace is headquartered in Amsterdam. Geneva hosts WHO, WTO and ILO; Nairobi hosts UNEP; Bonn hosts the UNFCCC secretariat.
9.tq: Greenpeace = Amsterdam; UNEP = Nairobi; UNFCCC = Bonn.

9.s: The United Nations Security Council consists of:
o: 15 members, comprising 5 permanent and 10 elected members
10 members, comprising 5 permanent and 5 elected members
17 members, comprising 5 permanent and 12 elected members
15 members, comprising 10 permanent and 5 elected members
9.x: The UNSC has 15 members: 5 permanent members and 10 members elected for two-year terms.
9.tq: Split the total into its permanent and elected components.

9.s: Under Article 97 of the UN Charter, the Secretary-General is appointed by:
o: The Economic and Social Council on the recommendation of the Security Council
The UN Security Council on the recommendation of the General Assembly
The International Court of Justice on the recommendation of the General Assembly
The UN General Assembly on the recommendation of the Security Council
9.x: Article 97 provides for appointment by the UN General Assembly upon the recommendation of the Security Council.
9.tq: Apply the 'who would do this job?' method to distinguish recommendation from appointment authority.

9.s:
Consider the following statements about the selection of the next UN Secretary-General:
1. Guterres demits office at the end of 2026 and the successor's term begins on 1 January 2027.
2. The successor gets a four-year term.
3. A candidate needs 9 'encourage' votes in the UNSC and no veto from the P5.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
9.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct as per the notes (straw polls in the UNSC; 9 'encourage' votes and no P5 veto). Statement 2 is wrong: the term is five years. So C (1 and 3 only) is right; A and B include statement 2; D includes all.
9.tq: UNSG: 5-year term, UNGA appoints on UNSC recommendation (Art. 97).

9.s:
Consider the following statements about the President of the 81st UN General Assembly (2026-27):
1. Khalilur Rahman of Bangladesh was elected.
2. It was the Asia-Pacific Group's turn.
3. He defeated a candidate from Greece.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
9.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Khalilur Rahman defeated Cyprus, not Greece. So A is right; B, C and D include statement 3.
9.tq: 81st UNGA: Khalilur Rahman (Bangladesh), Asia-Pacific turn, beat Cyprus.

9.s: Which one of the following lists contains all the countries elected to the Security Council for the 2027–28 term?
o: Austria, India, Portugal, Trinidad and Tobago, Zimbabwe
Austria, Kyrgyzstan, Japan, Trinidad and Tobago, Ghana
Austria, Kyrgyzstan, Portugal, Trinidad and Tobago, Zimbabwe
9.x: The countries elected for the 2027–28 term are Austria, Kyrgyzstan, Portugal, Trinidad and Tobago and Zimbabwe.
9.tq: Test complete list recall while using nearby states as membership traps.

9.s: The UN Security Council held its first-ever meeting on the risks posed by artificial intelligence to international peace in:
9.x: The first UNSC meeting on AI risks to peace was held in July 2023 (asked before). The other dates are distractors with no such first meeting.
9.tq: UNSC + AI first meeting = July 2023.

9.s: Rafael Grossi and Rebeca Grynspan, who held UNGA dialogues in April 2026 as candidates for UN Secretary-General, head respectively:
9.x: Rafael Grossi is DG of the IAEA and Rebeca Grynspan is SG of UNCTAD. C reverses them; WTO/ILO are Okonjo-Iweala/Houngbo and IMO/WMO are Dominguez/Saulo.
9.tq: UNSG 2026 candidates: Bachelet, Grynspan (UNCTAD), Sall, Grossi (IAEA).

9.s:
Consider the following statements about India's membership of UN bodies:
1. India was elected unopposed to the UN Human Rights Council for 2026-28.
2. This is India's seventh term on the UNHRC.
3. India was re-elected to the UNESCO Executive Board for 2026-28.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
9.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: India was elected unopposed to the UNHRC for 2026-28, for the 7th time. Statement 3 is wrong: India's UNESCO Executive Board term is 2025-29, not 2026-28. So A is right; B, C and D include statement 3.
9.tq: UNHRC 2026-28 (7th time); UNESCO Board 2025-29.

9.s: The ITU Council accepted India's bid to host which event in 2030?
o: The UN Commission on Narcotic Drugs
The World Summit on the Information Society in Tunis
9.x: The ITU Council accepted India's bid to host the ITU Plenipotentiary Conference 2030, known as PP-30.
9.tq: Match the host bid with the precise event name and abbreviation.

9.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Process or body)
 a. WSIS
 b. WSIS+20 review
 c. UN CERD
 d. WHA79

List-II (Associated fact)
 i. First review of India since 2007
 ii. Adopted the Global Action Plan on AMR 2026–2036
 iii. Geneva 2003 and Tunis 2005
 iv. Twenty-year review of the World Summit on the Information Society

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
9.x: WSIS was held in Geneva in 2003 and Tunis in 2005; WSIS+20 is its twenty-year review; UN CERD conducted its first review of India since 2007; and WHA79 adopted the AMR action plan.
9.tq: Start with the distinctive date pair for WSIS and use elimination for the remaining institutional links.

9.s: India was re-elected to the ICAO Council for the period
9.x: India was re-elected to the ICAO Council for the 2025-2028 period.
9.tq: Distinguish the exact institutional term from nearby three-year periods.

9.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the WHO Pandemic Agreement:
1. It was adopted on 20 May 2025.
2. Its PABS annex has already been agreed.
3. Talks on the PABS annex resumed in Geneva in July 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The PABS annex, concerning Pathogen Access and Benefit-Sharing, was still not agreed.
9.tq: Find the statement that reverses the status of an unfinished international agreement.

9.s: PABS, referred to in connection with the WHO Pandemic Agreement, stands for:
9.x: PABS stands for Pathogen Access and Benefit-Sharing.
9.tq: Test the exact expansion of a specialised international abbreviation.

9.s: The Global Action Plan on Antimicrobial Resistance for 2026–2036 was adopted at:
9.x: The 79th World Health Assembly, held in May 2026, adopted the Global Action Plan on AMR 2026–2036.
9.tq: Match the initiative with the adopting international forum and year.

9.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Fiji — 26th country to eliminate trachoma, October 2025
9.x: India was certified polio-free in 2014, not malaria-free. Cabo Verde, Fiji and Sri Lanka are correctly matched with the stated certifications.
9.tq: Identify the swapped disease certification in a country–achievement pair.

9.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Country)
 a. Bhutan
 b. Chile
 c. Niger
 d. Timor-Leste

List-II (WHO certification or validation)
 i. Malaria-free
 ii. First in the Americas to eliminate leprosy
 iii. First in the WHO South-East Asia Region to eliminate dog-transmitted rabies
 iv. First in Africa and fifth in the world to end onchocerciasis

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
9.x: Bhutan was the first in the WHO South-East Asia Region to eliminate dog-transmitted rabies; Chile was first in the Americas to eliminate leprosy; Niger ended onchocerciasis; and Timor-Leste became malaria-free.
9.tq: Start from the sure country–certification pair and eliminate the remaining codes.

9.s:
Consider the following statements about polio:
1. Wild poliovirus is now endemic only in Pakistan and Afghanistan.
2. WHO declared the end of Indonesia's type-2 polio outbreak.
3. India was certified polio-free in 2016.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
9.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct as per the notes. Statement 3 is wrong: India was certified polio-free in 2014 (2016 is Sri Lanka's malaria-free year). So A (1 and 2 only) is right; B, C and D include the wrong statement 3.
9.tq: India polio-free 2014; Sri Lanka malaria-free 2016 - don't mix them.

9.s: India's position in the negotiations relating to the WHO Pandemic Agreement is associated with its support for
9.x: India backs the developing-country Group for Equity in the negotiations on the WHO Pandemic Agreement.
9.tq: Identify the correct negotiating group rather than a similarly named international grouping.

9.s:
Match List-I (INTERPOL notice) with List-II (purpose):
List-I
a. Red Notice
b. Blue Notice
c. Yellow Notice
d. Silver Notice
List-II
i. Trace criminal assets
ii. Missing persons
iii. Locate and arrest a wanted person pending extradition
iv. Information on a person's identity, location or activities
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
9.x: Red = locate and arrest pending extradition (iii); Blue = information on identity/location/activities (iv); Yellow = missing persons (ii); Silver, the newest (2025) = trace criminal assets (i). Hence A. B swaps Red and Blue and Yellow/Silver; C swaps Blue and Yellow; D swaps Red and Silver.
9.tq: Silver = money (assets), Yellow = missing, Red = arrest.

9.s:
Consider the following statements regarding INTERPOL in India:
1. INTERPOL is headquartered at Lyon.
2. The Central Bureau of Investigation is India's National Central Bureau for INTERPOL.
3. The CBI seeks Red Notices.
4. A Blue Notice was issued for the Goa nightclub owners after a fire killed 25 people.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: All four statements are correct. INTERPOL's headquarters is in Lyon, the CBI is India's National Central Bureau, it seeks Red Notices, and a Blue Notice was issued in the stated Goa case.
9.tq: Combine headquarters, national agency, notice type and a current application in one question.

9.s: Which INTERPOL notice is used to locate and arrest a wanted person pending extradition?
9.x: A Red Notice is used to locate and arrest a wanted person pending extradition.
9.tq: Test the purpose of the notice rather than confusing its colour with another notice.

9.s: The newest INTERPOL notice, introduced in 2025, is intended to:
o: Seek information about a person's activities
9.x: The Silver Notice, introduced as the newest notice in 2025, is used to trace criminal assets.
9.tq: Use the year and purpose together to identify the newly introduced notice.

9.s: The Colombo Process is best described as:
o: A regional forum of Asian labour-sending countries on overseas employment
An INTERPOL system for tracing criminal assets
A WEF initiative on global economic restructuring
A UN mechanism for electing non-permanent members
9.x: The Colombo Process is a regional forum of Asian labour-sending countries concerned with overseas employment.
9.tq: Identify the forum by its membership base and subject area.

9.s: The ‘Great Reset’ is an initiative of the:
9.x: The Great Reset was a World Economic Forum initiative launched in 2020.
9.tq: Apply the organisation–initiative association trap.

9.s:
Consider the following statements about the International Solar Alliance:
1. It was launched by India and France at COP21 in 2015.
2. Its secretariat is in New Delhi.
3. Romania ratified its Framework Agreement in 2026.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
9.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the ISA secretariat is at Gurugram (New Delhi hosts CDRI). So C is right; A and B include statement 2; D includes all.
9.tq: ISA = Gurugram; CDRI = New Delhi.

9.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Kimberley Process — conflict-diamond certification — no headquarters
Global Biofuels Alliance — India's G20 — biofuels
9.x: CDRI was sponsored by India in 2019 and is headquartered in New Delhi. Japan and Tokyo are not its sponsor and secretariat combination.
9.tq: Detect the swapped sponsor and location in an initiative-based pairing.

9.s: The Kimberley Process is primarily associated with:
9.x: The Kimberley Process, established in 2003 by governments, industry and civil society, operates the Kimberley Process Certification Scheme for conflict diamonds and has no headquarters.
9.tq: Infer the initiative from its stated objective rather than from its institutional participants.

9.s: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) is jointly sponsored by:
9.x: The IPCC is sponsored by UNEP and WMO. Its AR6 synthesis report was released on 20 March 2023, and its AR7 cycle began in July 2023.
9.tq: Match the scientific body with its sponsoring organisations.

9.s: Which one of the following correctly describes POWERR Asia?
o: A Japan-sponsored initiative under AZEC Plus, launched in April 2026 for energy resilience, with India as a participant
A UNEP climate assessment cycle beginning in July 2023
An India-sponsored food-security programme launched at WTO MC14
An FAO treaty on plant genetic resources
9.x: POWERR Asia was sponsored by Japan under AZEC Plus in April 2026, focuses on energy resilience and includes India as a participant.
9.tq: Combine sponsor, framework, date, objective and participation in a single identification question.

9.s: The International Treaty on Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture, also known as the “Seed Treaty”, is sponsored by:
9.x: The ITPGRFA is sponsored by FAO and concerns plant genetic resources in harmony with the Convention on Biological Diversity.
9.tq: Use the common name and objective to identify the sponsoring organisation.

9.s: Which of the following countries joined BRICS from 1 January 2024?
o: Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and the United Arab Emirates
Argentina, Indonesia, Saudi Arabia and Egypt
Ethiopia, Saudi Arabia, Indonesia and the United Arab Emirates
9.x: Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and the United Arab Emirates joined BRICS from 1 January 2024. Argentina declined the invitation, while Indonesia joined in 2025 and Saudi Arabia's status remained unconfirmed.
9.tq: Use the exact admission date and separate invited, admitted and unconfirmed members.

9.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: New Development Bank — Chair in 2026: Uzbekistan
9.x: Bangladesh is the BIMSTEC chair for 2026. The other pairings incorrectly assign leadership roles not stated for those organisations.
9.tq: Find the organisation–current chair pair rather than confusing membership with chairmanship.

9.s: Bulgaria and Romania became full members of the Schengen Area from:
9.x: Bulgaria and Romania became full members of the Schengen Area on 1 January 2025.
9.tq: Use the precise date to distinguish partial or earlier accession from full membership.

9.s: Which of the following correctly describes the composition of the G20 as given in the current grouping?
o: 19 countries, the European Union and the African Union
19 countries and only the African Union
18 countries, the European Union and ASEAN
9.x: The grouping consists of 19 countries, the European Union and the African Union. The African Union became a member in 2023.
9.tq: Avoid the numerical trap by separating countries from regional organisations.

9.s:
Consider the following statements about the Kimberley Process:
1. It consists of 59 countries and the European Union.
2. India is a founding member.
3. India assumed its chairmanship from 1 January 2026 for the third time.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: The Kimberley Process comprises 60 participants—59 countries and the European Union. India is a founding member and took over its chairmanship on 1 January 2026 for the third time.
9.tq: Convert a composition figure and leadership details into a coded statement question.

9.s:
Consider the following statements about APEC:
1. India is a full member of APEC.
2. APEC has 21 economies and its Secretariat is in Singapore.
3. The 2025 APEC summit was held at Gyeongju, South Korea.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
9.x: Statement 1 is wrong: India is NOT a member of APEC, only an observer. Statements 2 and 3 are correct: 21 economies, Secretariat Singapore, 2025 summit at Gyeongju. So '2 and 3 only' (B) is right; A and D wrongly include 1, C wrongly drops 2.
9.tq: Remember the trap: India is only an observer in APEC.

9.s: Pax Silica, which India joined in February 2026, is associated primarily with:
o: Critical minerals, semiconductors and artificial-intelligence supply chains
International civil aviation and airport security
Nuclear disarmament and strategic arms reduction
9.x: Pax Silica is a US-led initiative concerning critical minerals, semiconductor supply chains and artificial intelligence supply chains.
9.tq: Identify the sector governed by the initiative instead of its geographical or political label.

9.s: Which country is the sixth member of the Colombo Security Conclave, formed in 2020?
9.x: The Conclave comprises India, Sri Lanka, Maldives, Mauritius, Bangladesh and Seychelles, with Seychelles as the 6th member. Bangladesh is a member but not the sixth; Myanmar and Indonesia are not members.
9.tq: CSC 6th member = Seychelles.

9.s: Which one of the following statements about NATO's enlargement is correct?
o: Finland became the 31st member in 2023 and Sweden the 32nd in 2024
Sweden became the 31st member in 2023 and Finland the 32nd in 2024
NATO has 30 members after Finland's entry
Finland and Sweden joined together on the same day in 2024
9.x: After the Ukraine war, Finland joined as the 31st member (2023) and Sweden as the 32nd (2024), taking NATO to 32. B reverses the order; C and D are wrong on count and dates.
9.tq: Finland 31st (2023), Sweden 32nd (2024).

9.s:
With reference to BRICS expansion, consider the following statements:
1. Argentina was invited at Johannesburg in August 2023 but declined.
2. Saudi Arabia was invited but has not formally joined.
3. Indonesia joined from 1 January 2024.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
9.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Indonesia joined only in January 2025; the 1 January 2024 entrants were Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and UAE. So B; C and D include 3, A misses 2.
9.tq: BRICS trap: Argentina declined, Saudi unconfirmed, Indonesia 2025.

9.s: The Chicago Convention of 1944 is primarily concerned with:
9.x: The Chicago Convention of 1944 governs international civil aviation and led to the creation of the International Civil Aviation Organization.
9.tq: Match each convention with its governing sector rather than its date alone.

9.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Basel Convention — prior informed consent for hazardous chemicals
9.x: The Vienna Convention of 1985 concerns protection of the ozone layer. Rotterdam concerns prior informed consent for hazardous chemicals, Basel concerns transboundary hazardous waste, and the Windsor Framework concerns post-Brexit UK–EU trade rules for Northern Ireland.
9.tq: Discriminate among conventions dealing with closely related environmental and trade subjects.

9.s: The Hague Conventions administered through HCCH primarily deal with:
9.x: The Hague Conventions under HCCH concern private international law, including the Apostille Convention of 1961 and the Child Abduction Convention of 1980.
9.tq: Use the subject-area clue to distinguish private international law from public international organisations.

9.s: Which convention governs the transboundary movement of hazardous waste?
9.x: The Basel Convention of 1989 governs transboundary hazardous waste. It also includes a plastic-waste amendment and stronger rules relating to e-waste.
9.tq: Match the convention to its core regulatory object and avoid confusing adjacent environmental treaties.

9.s: The Stockholm Convention of 2001 primarily concerns:
9.x: The Stockholm Convention deals with persistent organic pollutants. The listed framework covers 34 chemicals, including recently noted substances such as chlorpyrifos and PFAS.
9.tq: Use the exact environmental category—POPs—to separate Stockholm from Basel and Minamata.

9.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the Minamata Convention?
o: Mercury; dental amalgam to be phased out by 2034
9.x: The Minamata Convention of 2013 concerns mercury, and dental amalgam is to be phased out by 2034. POPs belong to the Stockholm Convention and hazardous waste to the Basel Convention.
9.tq: Start from the sure substance–treaty pair and eliminate the swapped environmental categories.

9.s: The Windsor Framework of 2023 governs:
o: UK–EU post-Brexit trade rules for Northern Ireland
The global trade in hazardous chemicals
The admission of new NATO members
9.x: The Windsor Framework establishes UK–EU post-Brexit trade arrangements for Northern Ireland.
9.tq: Identify the geographic and political parties governed by the framework.

9.s:
Arrange the following conventions/frameworks in chronological order of adoption:
A. Minamata Convention
B. Chicago Convention
C. Stockholm Convention
D. Basel Convention
9.x: The correct sequence is Chicago Convention (1944), Basel Convention (1989), Stockholm Convention (2001), and Minamata Convention (2013).
9.tq: Place the earliest and latest dates first, then resolve the middle sequence.

9.s:
Consider the following statements about the Water Convention:
1. It was adopted at Helsinki in 1992.
2. It entered into force in 1996.
3. It concerns transboundary rivers and lakes.
4. Bangladesh became the first South Asian party.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: All four statements are correct. The Helsinki Water Convention was adopted in 1992, entered into force in 1996, concerns transboundary waters, and Bangladesh was the first South Asian party.
9.tq: Verify the place, dates, subject and regional accession status independently.

9.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Convention on Nuclear Safety — India became a party in 2016
Convention on Supplementary Compensation — India became a party in 2016
Convention on Supplementary Compensation — adopted in 1997; entered into force in 2015
Convention on Nuclear Safety — adopted in 1994; entered into force in 1996
9.x: India is a party to the Convention on Nuclear Safety, but the 2016 accession detail applies to the Convention on Supplementary Compensation (CSC).
9.tq: Find the swapped date or status in a set of closely related nuclear conventions.

9.s: With reference to the five United Nations outer-space treaties, which one of the following is correct regarding India?
o: India has ratified all five but signed only four.
India has signed and ratified all five.
India has signed all five and ratified four, but not the Moon Agreement of 1979.
India has neither signed nor ratified the Moon Agreement but has ratified only three others.
9.x: India has signed all five UN outer-space treaties and ratified four. The exception is the 1979 Moon Agreement, which India has not ratified.
9.tq: Separate the complete signature record from the incomplete ratification record.

9.s: Which one of the following statements about the Montreal Protocol is correct?
o: It was replaced by the Chicago Convention in 2026.
It has been ratified by 90 parties and is not universally ratified.
It has been ratified by 197 parties and is universally ratified.
India will stop all HFC production immediately under the original protocol.
9.x: The Montreal Protocol is universally ratified by 197 parties. India is to stop clearances for new HFC production beyond 31 December 2027 under the Kigali Amendment.
9.tq: Use the ratification-count and universal-status clue while rejecting unrelated treaty substitutions.

9.s: Under the Kigali Amendment, India will stop clearances for new HFC production beyond
9.x: India will stop clearances for new hydrofluorocarbon production beyond 31 December 2027 under the Kigali Amendment.
9.tq: Recall the precise deadline rather than the year of adoption of the parent protocol.

9.s: The United States announced its intention to quit how many international bodies, comprising non-UN and UN bodies respectively?
9.x: The United States announced its intention to quit 66 bodies—35 non-UN bodies and 31 UN bodies. The listed bodies included WHO, UNFCCC, IPCC, ISA, IRENA, UNHRC and UNESCO.
9.tq: Retain the total and its two-part numerical breakdown together.

9.s:
With reference to the BBNJ or High Seas Treaty, consider the following statements:
1. It was adopted in March 2023.
2. It entered into force on 17 January 2026.
3. India has ratified the treaty.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: The BBNJ Treaty was adopted in March 2023 and entered into force on 17 January 2026. India has signed but not ratified it.
9.tq: Find the incorrect accession-status statement; signing and ratification are distinct stages.

9.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the UN Convention against Cybercrime is correct?
o: India signed it at Hanoi in October 2025.
India did not sign it, citing concerns relating to privacy and data sovereignty.
India ratified it immediately after its adoption in December 2024.
It was negotiated under the International Civil Aviation Organization.
9.x: India did not sign the UN Convention against Cybercrime because of concerns relating to privacy and data sovereignty.
9.tq: Use the country-status and stated-reason trap in an international agreement question.

9.s:
Consider the following statements about the UN Convention against Cybercrime:
1. It was adopted by the UN General Assembly in December 2024 and is the first global cybercrime treaty.
2. It was opened for signature at Hanoi in October 2025.
3. It becomes binding 90 days after 40 ratifications.
4. Its secretariat is UNCTAD.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct (UNGA Res. 79/243, Dec 2024; Hanoi, Oct 2025; binding 90 days after 40 ratifications). Statement 4 is wrong: the secretariat is UNODC, not UNCTAD. So B is right; A omits 3; C and D include the wrong statement 4.
9.tq: Cybercrime = crime, so the secretariat is UNODC.

9.s: The First Additional Protocol to the India-MERCOSUR Preferential Trade Agreement, signed in September 2026, relates to
9.x: The First Additional Protocol concerns electronic certificates of origin.
9.tq: Match the agreement with its specific subject instead of its broader trade category.

9.s: The Washington Accords, signed on 4 December 2025, concern
o: the regulation of high seas biodiversity
trade between the United Kingdom and the European Union
peace between the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda
9.x: The Washington Accords are a United States-brokered peace agreement between the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda.
9.tq: Use the parties-and-purpose approach to distinguish similarly named international agreements.

9.s:
Consider the following statements about the U.S. exit from international bodies announced in January 2026:
1. It included the UNFCCC, IPCC and IRENA.
2. The U.S. was described as the first country to attempt formal withdrawal from the UNFCCC.
3. The International Solar Alliance was not among the bodies the U.S. exited.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
9.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct as per the notes. Statement 3 is wrong: the ISA was among the bodies the U.S. exited (along with UNFPA, UN Women, UNHRC, UNCTAD). So A is right; B, C and D include statement 3.
9.tq: The U.S. exit list did include the India-founded ISA.

9.s: In India, treaties are concluded in the name of the
9.x: Treaties concluded by India are concluded in the name of the President. Article 253 empowers Parliament to legislate for their implementation.
9.tq: Apply the ‘who performs this constitutional function?’ method.

9.s: Article 253 of the Constitution of India enables Parliament to
o: appoint the secretariat of every UN convention
ratify every treaty without executive action
withdraw India from any treaty without consultation
legislate for implementing treaties and international agreements
9.x: Article 253 empowers Parliament to make laws for implementing treaties, agreements and conventions with foreign countries or decisions made at international conferences.
9.tq: Apply the constitutional provision to the practical task of treaty implementation.

9.s: The United States' exit from UNESCO announced in January 2026 was its:
9.x: The January 2026 US memorandum to quit 66 bodies included UNESCO, its third exit after 1984 and 2017. A and B undercount; D adds a non-existent exit.
9.tq: US-UNESCO exits: 1984, 2017, 2026.

9.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
9.x: India signed the CEPA with the UAE in 2022. ECTA was with Australia, TEPA with EFTA and CETA with the UK.
9.tq: Start with the sure partner-agreement pair and eliminate swapped partners.

9.s: India's first Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) in the Gulf Cooperation Council region was signed with
9.x: The 2022 CEPA with the United Arab Emirates was India's first CEPA in the GCC region.
9.tq: Distinguish the first regional agreement from the later second GCC CEPA.

9.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the India-EFTA Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement (TEPA):
1. It was signed in March 2024.
2. It came into force on 1 October 2025.
3. The EFTA countries are Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: All three statements are correct. TEPA was signed in March 2024, entered into force on 1 October 2025, and involves the four EFTA countries listed.
9.tq: Check dates and the complete membership list before choosing the coded option.

9.s: The India-UK CETA was signed in July 2025 and came into force on
9.x: The India-UK CETA was signed in July 2025 and entered into force on 15 July 2026.
9.tq: Distinguish the agreement's signing month from its later entry-into-force date.

9.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The India-UK CETA has been described as a 'Gold standard' deal.
2. The India-EU FTA has been described as the 'Mother of All Deals'.
3. Under the India-EU FTA, 99% of India's exports become duty-free at once.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
9.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: under the India-EU FTA, 90.7% of India's exports become duty-free at once; 99% is the figure for the India-Oman CEPA. So A is right; B, C and D include statement 3.
9.tq: EU 90.7% at once; Oman 99%; UK = 'Gold standard'.

9.s: Which of the following statements regarding India's later trade agreements is correct?
o: The India-New Zealand FTA entered into force in June 2026.
The India-EU FTA was signed with EFTA as its partner.
Under the India-Oman CEPA, 99% of India's exports became duty-free.
The India-Oman CEPA was India's first GCC CEPA.
9.x: The India-Oman CEPA, signed in December 2025 and in force from June 2026, provides duty-free treatment for 99% of India's exports. It is India's second GCC CEPA.
9.tq: Find the precise trade concession while rejecting wrong first-agreement, date and partner claims.

9.s: India's Free Trade Agreement concluded with New Zealand was signed in
9.x: India and New Zealand signed an FTA in December 2025.
9.tq: Match the partner with the correct agreement type and date.

9.s:
The India-EU FTA is to operate along with which of the following?
1. An Investment Protection Agreement
2. A Geographical Indications Agreement
3. A Nuclear Liability Convention
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
9.x: The India-EU FTA is to operate with an Investment Protection Agreement and a Geographical Indications Agreement. A Nuclear Liability Convention is not mentioned as an accompanying instrument.
9.tq: Identify the two associated instruments and reject the unrelated treaty subject.

9.s: As of June 2026, India had how many FTAs covering how many countries?
9.x: India had 15 FTAs covering 27 countries as of June 2026.
9.tq: Keep the number of agreements separate from the number of partner countries.

9.s: In February 2026, India and the United States issued a joint statement on a trade deal. The United States referred to such deals as
9.x: The United States calls such trade arrangements “Agreements on Reciprocal Trade.”
9.tq: Identify the exact official terminology used by the negotiating country.

9.s: Which WTO subsidy box covers trade-distorting domestic support that is subject to a cap based on de minimis limits?
9.x: Amber Box subsidies are trade-distorting domestic support measures and are subject to prescribed limits, including de minimis ceilings.
9.tq: Use the exact subject-function association to distinguish the subsidy boxes.

9.s: Support tied to production-limiting programmes is classified under which WTO subsidy box?
9.x: Blue Box support is linked to programmes that limit production.
9.tq: Discriminate between the closely related Amber, Blue and Green subsidy categories.

9.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Green Box measures are regarded as having minimal or no trade distortion.
2. Green Box support is not subject to a cap.
3. Green Box measures are exclusively related to intellectual property rights.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: Green Box measures have minimal or no trade-distorting effects and are not capped. Intellectual property rights are covered by TRIPS, not the Green Box.
9.tq: Find the statement that swaps a subsidy category with a neighbouring WTO agreement.

9.s: TRIMs is concerned with:
9.x: TRIMs refers to Trade-Related Investment Measures.
9.tq: Separate look-alike WTO acronyms by their exact subject.

9.s: Which one of the following statements regarding GATT is correct?
o: It was signed in 1994 and came into force in 1995.
It was signed in 1947 and came into force in 1948.
It was signed in 1986 and came into force in 1991.
It was signed in 1948 and came into force in 1947.
9.x: The General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade was signed in 1947 and entered into force in 1948.
9.tq: Use the chronological pair to catch a reversal of the signing and enforcement years.

9.s: The Most-Favoured-Nation clause is associated with which of the following?
9.x: The Most-Favoured-Nation clause is a fundamental principle associated with GATT.
9.tq: Match a distinctive principle with the correct international agreement.

9.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Uruguay Round was the eighth round of multilateral trade negotiations under GATT.
2. It commenced in 1986.
3. It resulted in the creation of the WTO on 1 January 1995.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: The Uruguay Round was the eighth GATT round, began in 1986 and led to the WTO, which came into existence on 1 January 1995.
9.tq: Combine the round number, starting year and institutional outcome in one statement set.

9.s: The Dunkel Draft of 1991 was associated with proposals made by:
9.x: The Dunkel Draft contained proposals made by Arthur Dunkel, the Director-General of GATT, during the Uruguay Round.
9.tq: Use the person–institution–document association rather than a general economic personality link.

9.s: The Peace Clause agreed at Bali in 2013 primarily protects developing countries from WTO disputes concerning:
9.x: The Bali Peace Clause shields developing countries' public food-stockholding programmes from disputes over Amber Box limits until a permanent solution is found.
9.tq: Apply the agreement to the specific policy situation it was designed to protect.

9.s: Which pair is correctly matched?
9.x: The IMF formally came into existence on 27 December 1945, while its operations began on 1 March 1947.
9.tq: Separate closely spaced institutional dates by matching each date with the correct event.

9.s: The first borrower from the International Monetary Fund was:
9.x: France was the first country to borrow from the IMF.
9.tq: Test the specific first-institutional-event fact against nearby country names.

9.s: Which of the following is the private-sector arm of the World Bank Group?
9.x: The International Finance Corporation is the private-sector arm of the World Bank Group and has 184 members.
9.tq: Identify the institutional mandate hidden among similar abbreviations.

9.s:
Consider the following statements about IMF lending:
1. The IMF lends only to its member countries.
2. Its lending is intended to address balance-of-payments problems.
3. The Rapid Financing Instrument requires a full economic programme in every case.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: The IMF lends only to members and primarily addresses balance-of-payments problems. The Rapid Financing Instrument provides quick liquidity without requiring a full programme.
9.tq: Locate the reversed condition in a statement about an institutional lending instrument.

9.s: Which IMF facility was associated with the softest terms?
9.x: The Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility, or ESAF, had the softest terms among the facilities mentioned.
9.tq: Distinguish concessionality from speed and from the mandates of other institutions.

9.s: Which combination best describes the structural adjustment programmes of the 1980s and 1990s?
o: Debt cancellation, disarmament and refugee resettlement
Public food stocking, tariff abolition and gold accumulation
Universal subsidies, nationalisation and currency appreciation
9.x: Structural adjustment programmes commonly involved austerity, privatisation and devaluation; studies linked them to rising poverty and inequality in the Global South.
9.tq: Identify the complete policy cluster associated with structural adjustment programmes.

9.s: Special Drawing Rights are best described as:
o: An IMF reserve asset commonly called “paper gold”
9.x: SDR is an IMF reserve asset, commonly referred to as “paper gold.” It is not a World Bank loan, WTO concession or UN grant.
9.tq: Distinguish an IMF reserve asset from lending, trade and development instruments of other bodies.

9.s:
The SDR basket comprises which of the following currencies?
1. United States dollar
2. Euro
3. Chinese yuan
4. Japanese yen
5. Pound sterling
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
9.x: The SDR basket consists of the U.S. dollar, euro, Chinese yuan, Japanese yen and pound sterling.
9.tq: Check the complete basket rather than stopping after identifying the first familiar currencies.

9.s:
Which of the following components form part of India's foreign exchange reserves as listed in the institutional description?
1. Foreign currency assets
2. Gold
3. SDRs
4. Reserve tranche or reserve position
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
9.x: The listed components are foreign currency assets, gold, SDRs and the reserve tranche or reserve position.
9.tq: Treat a reserve composition question as a complete-list test and check every component.

9.s:
Consider the following statements about BRICS and IMF voting:
1. In 2011, BRICS had about 20% of world GDP but only 11% of IMF votes.
2. BRICS now has about 40% of world GDP and its IMF vote share has roughly doubled.
3. The New Delhi Declaration seeks IMF quota and voting reform.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
9.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: BRICS has about 40% of world GDP but its vote share is only barely higher, not doubled. So C is right; A and B include statement 2; D includes all.
9.tq: The point of the BRICS complaint is that votes did NOT keep pace with GDP.

9.s: The SHANTI Act 2025 caps nuclear liability at:
9.x: The SHANTI Act 2025 caps nuclear liability at 300 million SDRs, stated as approximately ₹3,900 crore.
9.tq: Keep the unit SDR distinct from a dollar amount while checking the corresponding rupee approximation.

9.s:
Consider the following statements about the New Development Bank:
1. Its headquarters is in Beijing.
2. Uzbekistan became its 10th member and the first from Central Asia.
3. The founders' collective vote cannot fall below 55%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
9.x: Statement 1 is wrong: the NDB is headquartered in Shanghai. Statements 2 and 3 are correct as per the notes. So B (2 and 3 only) is right; A and D include statement 1; C omits statement 2.
9.tq: NDB: Shanghai, Fortaleza 2014, founders keep at least 55%.

9.s: Which one of the following statements about the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank is correct?
o: It was established in 2014 and has 55 approved members.
It was established in 2016 and has 111 approved members.
It was established in 2023 and has 184 approved members.
It was established in 1995 and has 29 approved members.
9.x: AIIB was established in 2016 and has 111 approved members.
9.tq: Match the institution’s founding year with its membership figure.

9.s: The BRICS Contingency Reserve Arrangement is intended to serve as:
o: A mechanism for intellectual property registration
A common agricultural subsidy fund of the WTO
An alternative source of IMF-type liquidity support for BRICS members
9.x: The BRICS Contingency Reserve Arrangement provides a BRICS alternative to IMF liquidity support.
9.tq: Infer the institutional purpose from the type of financial problem addressed.

9.s: Which of the following is a Maastricht criterion for entry into the Eurozone?
o: Public debt below 20% of GDP only
9.x: Eurozone entry criteria include a deficit below 3% of GDP, debt below 60% of GDP and participation in ERM II.
9.tq: Recognise the precise numerical threshold among reversed or incomplete criteria.

9.s: According to the stated development, which country became the 21st member of the Eurozone in 2026?
9.x: Bulgaria became the 21st member of the Eurozone in 2026 after meeting the Maastricht criteria.
9.tq: Test the newest-member fact against nearby European countries.

9.s: Which country joined the New Development Bank (NDB) in 2023?
9.x: Egypt joined the NDB (set up by the 2014 Fortaleza Declaration, HQ Shanghai) in 2023. Uzbekistan later became the 10th member and first from Central Asia. Argentina and Indonesia are BRICS-expansion names, not NDB entrants in the notes.
9.tq: NDB: Egypt 2023; Uzbekistan 10th.

9.s: Mission Schools of Excellence, involving AIIB and World Bank financing of ₹7,500 crore, is associated with:
9.x: Mission Schools of Excellence is associated with Gujarat and involves AIIB and World Bank financing of ₹7,500 crore.
9.tq: Combine the project, lender pair and State instead of relying on the project name alone.

9.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: NDB — SALT programme in Andhra Pradesh
IBRD — Mission Schools of Excellence in Gujarat
9.x: AIIB is associated with Mumbai Urban Transport Project-III. NDB is associated with the Delhi-Ghaziabad-Meerut RRTS, while SALT is a World Bank project in Andhra Pradesh.
9.tq: Catch the lender–project swap by comparing neighbouring multilateral-bank projects.

9.s: The Delhi-Ghaziabad-Meerut Regional Rapid Transit System is financed by:
9.x: The Delhi-Ghaziabad-Meerut RRTS is associated with NDB financing in collaboration with ADB and serves the National Capital Region.
9.tq: Identify the correct lender partnership rather than a single-bank association.

9.s: Approximately how much was facilitated by the Centre for Amaravati through the World Bank, ADB and HUDCO?
9.x: The Centre facilitated approximately ₹26,000 crore for Amaravati through the World Bank, ADB and HUDCO; ₹15,000 crore was separately fast-tracked as special assistance.
9.tq: Separate the total facilitated amount from the distinct special-assistance component.

9.s: In June 2023, which institution financed Bangladesh's Gazipur-Elenga (N4) and Natore-Nawabganj (N6) road-safety highway projects worth $358 million?
9.x: The World Bank financed these road-safety highways ($358 mn, June 2023), a question asked before. ADB, NDB and AIIB are other multilateral lenders not linked to this project in the notes.
9.tq: Bangladesh N4/N6 road safety = World Bank.

9.s: India became the world's fourth-largest economy in 2025 in terms of nominal GDP, with a size of approximately:
9.x: India was reported as the fourth-largest economy in 2025 with a nominal GDP of approximately $4.18 trillion, overtaking Japan.
9.tq: Link the ranking with the specific nominal GDP figure rather than a trade value.

9.s: India's reported position in the IMF ranking after the fall in the rupee was:
9.x: India was reported to have slipped to sixth place in the IMF ranking after the rupee's fall.
9.tq: Distinguish a later ranking change from the earlier fourth-place nominal GDP report.

9.s: In July 2026, Russia accounted for more than what share of India's oil imports?
9.x: Russia supplied more than 51% of India's oil imports in July 2026, an all-time high in the stated period.
9.tq: Distinguish the July peak from the earlier sub-20% share in January.

9.s: Which country was India's largest import source in 2024–25 among the following?
9.x: China was India's largest listed import source in 2024–25, accounting for 15.73%, followed by Russia, the UAE and the United States.
9.tq: Compare the percentages rather than relying on the geopolitical prominence of a country.

9.s: India's record remittances in FY 2024–25 were reported at approximately:
9.x: India received record remittances of approximately $135 billion in FY 2024–25.
9.tq: Distinguish the annual remittance total from the separate workers' remittance measure for FY26.

9.s: Foreign direct investment inflows in 2025 increased by 73% to approximately:
9.x: FDI inflows increased by 73% in 2025 to approximately $47 billion.
9.tq: Match the percentage increase with the correct resulting inflow amount.

9.s: According to the WTO, in 2024 India was the world's ____ largest exporter of commercial services.
9.x: India was the 8th largest exporter (4.3% share) and 9th largest importer (3.4%) of commercial services in 2024. 9th is its importer rank; 4th and 6th are its GDP ranks.
9.tq: Services: 8th exporter, 9th importer.

9.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
9.x: The World Economic Outlook is an IMF report. Global Economic Prospects, World Development Report and Human Capital Index are associated with the World Bank.
9.tq: Begin with the sure report-institution pair and eliminate reports belonging to neighbouring institutions.

9.s: Which one of the following statements about the World Bank's reports is correct?
o: Global Economic Prospects is issued in January and June, and India's FY26 forecast was raised to 7.2% from 6.3%
World Development Report 2025 is titled Standards for Development and is an IMF report
Human Capital Index is a report of UNCTAD
Global Economic Prospects is issued only once every five years
9.x: Global Economic Prospects is issued in January and June, and the cited India FY26 forecast was raised from 6.3% to 7.2%. World Development Report 2025 is titled Standards for Development and is also associated with the World Bank.
9.tq: Check both the publication frequency and the forecast figures before accepting the complete statement.

9.s: Which institution projected India's growth at 6.6 per cent for 2026-27 in June 2026?
9.x: The Reserve Bank of India projected India's growth at 6.6 per cent for 2026-27 in June 2026.
9.tq: Match the agency directly with its forecast.

9.s: With reference to the IMF's projections for India, which one of the following is correct?
o: 2025-26 was raised to 7.3 per cent and FY27 was projected at about 6.2 per cent.
2025-26 was raised to 6.2 per cent and FY27 was projected at 7.3 per cent.
2025-26 was projected at 6.6 per cent and FY27 at 7.2 per cent.
Both 2025-26 and FY27 were projected at 7.3 per cent.
9.x: The IMF raised its 2025-26 projection to 7.3 per cent in January 2026 and projected about 6.2 per cent for FY27 in April 2026.
9.tq: Separate the agency, year and direction of revision before choosing.

9.s: Which of the following correctly describes S&P's assessment of India?
o: India was upgraded from BBB- to BBB in 2025, the first such upgrade in nearly two decades, and BBB was affirmed in September 2026.
India was upgraded from BBB to BBB- in 2025.
India received an AAA rating for the first time in 2025.
India was downgraded from BBB to BBB- in September 2026.
9.x: S&P upgraded India from BBB- to BBB in 2025, its first upgrade in nearly two decades, and affirmed the BBB rating in September 2026.
9.tq: Watch for reversed rating movements and swapped rating grades.

9.s: India's growth during the period under consideration was driven mainly by which combination?
o: Foreign aid and reduction in public investment
Strong private consumption and public investment
9.x: The principal growth drivers identified were strong private consumption and public investment.
9.tq: Identify the precise cause-effect combination rather than a broad growth claim.

9.s: The theme of the World Development Report 2025 was:
9.x: The World Development Report 2025 carried the theme “Standards for Development” and was published by the World Bank.
9.tq: Use the exact official wording of the report theme instead of a similar economic phrase.

9.s: Which organisation has published the World Investment Report since 1991?
9.x: The World Investment Report has been published by the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development since 1991.
9.tq: Match the report with its specialised international publisher and institutional history.

9.s: Which of the following statements about the World Investment Report 2026 is correct?
o: Its theme was ‘The Promise of AI’ and global FDI rose by 16%.
Its theme was ‘Off Target’ and global FDI declined to $1.6 trillion.
Its theme was ‘International Investment in a Turbulent Era’ and global FDI was $1.6 trillion, up 6%.
Its theme was ‘Standards for Development’ and global FDI was $6 trillion.
9.x: The World Investment Report 2026 carried the theme ‘International Investment in a Turbulent Era’ and reported global FDI of $1.6 trillion, an increase of 6%.
9.tq: Separate the report theme, publisher-linked subject and quantitative finding.

9.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Corruption Perceptions Index — World Economic Forum
Travel and Tourism Development Index — Transparency International
9.x: The Logistics Performance Index is published by the World Bank. The Corruption Perceptions Index is published by Transparency International, while the Global Gender Gap and Travel and Tourism Development indices are associated with the World Economic Forum.
9.tq: Begin with the World Bank's distinctive logistics-related index and eliminate publisher swaps.

9.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the World Bank's Global Economic Prospects projections of June 2026 for India and the world?
9.x: The June 2026 Global Economic Prospects projected India's FY27 growth at 6.6%, FY26 at 7.7% and FY28 at 7.2%; world growth was projected at 2.5% in 2026.
9.tq: Read the figures across a comparison table without reversing years.

9.s: Sarnath became India's which numbered World Heritage Site in July 2026?
9.x: Sarnath became India's 45th World Heritage Site in July 2026.
9.tq: Use the exact ordinal number associated with the current-affairs development.

9.s: Which of the following developments was identified as weakening multilateralism?
o: The failure of MC14 and withdrawals by the United States
The creation of the World Development Report
The launch of the SDR basket
The success of MC14 and the expansion of the Appellate Body
9.x: The failure of MC14 and U.S. exits were identified as developments weakening multilateralism.
9.tq: Link the criticism to the stated institutional outcome rather than to an unrelated economic report.

9.s:
India's refusal to join which of the following has been defended as protecting policy space?
1. Investment Facilitation for Development
2. Cybercrime Convention
3. Pandemic Agreement
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
9.x: India's refusals concerning the Investment Facilitation for Development initiative and the Cybercrime Convention have been defended as protecting policy space. The Pandemic Agreement is discussed separately because its PABS annex remains incomplete.
9.tq: Separate the instruments India refused from the agreement whose annex is still pending.

9.s:
Which of the following international roles is associated with India in 2026?
1. Chair of the Kimberley Process
2. Host of ITU PP-30
3. Founder of ISA, CDRI and GBA
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
9.x: India's listed roles include chairing the Kimberley Process in 2026, hosting ITU PP-30 and being a founder of the ISA, CDRI and GBA.
9.tq: Test a cluster of related international roles through a complete-list statement question.

9.s: The lapse of the WTO e-commerce moratorium was associated with which development?
o: The creation of the SDR basket in 2026
The India–UK CETA coming into force in July 2026
9.x: The failure of MC14 and the lapse of the e-commerce moratorium were reported in March 2026.
9.tq: Pair the event with its specific WTO context and time rather than with another trade agreement.

9.s: The IMF and World Bank growth projections were cut during April–June 2026 primarily because of:
o: India's CETA with the United Kingdom
The lapse of the e-commerce moratorium
9.x: The growth cuts by the IMF and World Bank during April–June 2026 were attributed to the West Asia war.
9.tq: Identify the stated cause-and-effect link behind a change in economic projections.

9.s: The World Bank road and school projects in Andhra Pradesh are referred to as:
9.x: The World Bank road and school projects in Andhra Pradesh are referred to as SALT projects.
9.tq: Match the project acronym with its sectoral and geographical context.

9.s: Which one of the following correctly reflects the criticism concerning the WTO and the Bretton Woods institutions?
o: The criticism concerns only the UNFCCC and not the WTO.
The WTO Appellate Body has been fully restored and India has accepted IFD without reservation.
Bretton Woods institutions have abolished quota-based voting.
The WTO Appellate Body is paralysed, India is blocking IFD, and Bretton Woods voting imbalance remains a concern.
9.x: The stated criticisms concern WTO paralysis through the Appellate Body, India's blocking of IFD and continuing voting imbalance in the Bretton Woods institutions.
9.tq: Select the option that preserves all parts of a multi-issue institutional criticism without reversing them.

10.s: Which one of the following correctly describes India's Act East Policy?
o: It was launched in 1991 and focuses on the Gulf and West Asia for energy and diaspora links.
It began in 2014 and was later renamed Look East in 1991.
It was upgraded from the Look East Policy (1991) in 2014 and focuses on strategic ties with ASEAN, Japan and South Korea.
It originated with SAARC leaders at the Prime Minister's swearing-in in 2014 and focuses on disaster response for neighbours.
10.x: C is correct: Look East (1991) was upgraded to Act East in 2014, focusing on ASEAN, Japan and South Korea. A describes Link West. B reverses the chronology. D describes Neighbourhood First.
10.tq: Look East 1991 -> Act East 2014; East = ASEAN/Japan/Korea, West = Gulf.

10.s:
Consider the following statements about India's Neighbourhood First policy:
1. Its origin is associated with the presence of SAARC leaders at the Prime Minister's swearing-in in 2014.
2. It gives priority to aid, infrastructure, connectivity and disaster response for neighbouring countries.
3. It mainly concerns energy and diaspora links with the Gulf and West Asia.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
10.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct as per the notes. Statement 3 is wrong: Gulf/West Asia energy and diaspora links are the focus of Link West, not Neighbourhood First. Hence 1 and 2 only; options containing 3 are wrong, and 1 only misses statement 2.
10.tq: Neighbourhood First = SAARC leaders at 2014 swearing-in; Gulf = Link West.

10.s: The Link West policy primarily concerns India’s relations with which region and interests?
o: Gulf and West Asia, especially energy and diaspora links
Central Asia, with emphasis on space cooperation
Europe, with emphasis on agricultural subsidies
10.x: Link West focuses on the Gulf and West Asia, particularly energy interests and diaspora links.
10.tq: Use the doctrine’s geographic label and its two stated policy interests together.

10.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. SAGAR (2015) stands for Security and Growth for All in the Region.
2. MAHASAGAR (2025) extends the scope of SAGAR to Central Asia and Eurasia.
3. SAGAR envisages India as a net security provider in the Indian Ocean Region.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
10.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: MAHASAGAR (2025) extends SAGAR to the Global South and the Indo-Pacific, not Central Asia. Statement 3 is correct: SAGAR casts India as net security provider in the IOR. So 1 and 3 only.
10.tq: SAGAR 2015 (IOR) -> MAHASAGAR 2025 (Global South + Indo-Pacific).

10.s: SHANTI, introduced in 2026, refers to which of the following?
o: Security and Humanitarian Assistance for Neighbourhood, Technology and Inclusion
Securing Holistic Advancement through Norms, Trust, and Integrity
Sustainable Humanitarian Action for New Trade Initiatives
Strategic Harmony and Alliance for Navigation, Trade and Investment
10.x: SHANTI stands for Securing Holistic Advancement through Norms, Trust, and Integrity and relates to cooperative maritime security in the Bay of Bengal.
10.tq: Test the exact expansion of an acronym and connect it to its policy domain.

10.s: The Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative (IPOI) was launched at which venue and consists of how many pillars?
10.x: IPOI originated at the East Asia Summit in Bangkok in 2019 and has seven pillars.
10.tq: Combine the launch venue, year and numerical feature of a regional initiative.

10.s: Which of the following correctly states the principal features of India’s nuclear doctrine as identified in the Group-II framework?
o: No First Use and credible minimum deterrence, formulated in 2003
First Use and maximum deterrence, formulated in 1991
No First Use and zero deterrence, formulated in 2014
Flexible First Use and unlimited deterrence, formulated in 2019
10.x: India’s nuclear doctrine is associated with 2003 and includes No First Use and credible minimum deterrence.
10.tq: Match the doctrine with its date and two defining principles while rejecting reversed terminology.

10.s: Which one of the following statements about the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) is correct?
o: It was founded at Bandung in 1955 and meant strict neutrality in world affairs.
It was founded at Belgrade in 1961 by leaders including Nehru, Tito, Nasser, Nkrumah and Sukarno, and non-alignment was not mere neutrality.
It was founded at Belgrade in 1961 and committed members to permanent neutrality.
It was founded at Cairo in 1964 by Nehru, Tito and Nasser alone.
10.x: B is correct: NAM was founded at Belgrade in 1961 by Nehru, Tito, Nasser, Nkrumah and Sukarno, and non-alignment is not the same as neutrality. A gives the wrong place/year and the neutrality trap; C has the right place but repeats the neutrality trap; D gives the wrong place and year.
10.tq: NAM = Belgrade 1961; trap: non-alignment is not neutrality.

10.s: Which one of the following statements about the 16th India-Japan Annual Summit (July 2026) is correct?
o: It was held in Tokyo and declared 2027 the Year of Shared Horizons marking 50 years of ties.

It was held in New Delhi, adopted a Joint Declaration on Economic Security (semiconductors, critical minerals, ICT, clean energy, pharma), and 2027 was named the Year of Shared Horizons marking 75 years of ties.
It was held in New Delhi and adopted a Joint Declaration on Defence and Security along with operationalising a civil nuclear deal.
It was held in New Delhi and concluded a free trade agreement making Japan India's 22nd FTA partner.
10.x: B is correct per the notes. A has the wrong venue and the wrong anniversary (75, not 50). C describes the India-Australia 3rd Annual Summit in Melbourne. D describes the EU, India's 22nd FTA partner.
10.tq: Japan 16th summit = New Delhi, Economic Security (5 sectors), 2027 = 75 years.

10.s:
With reference to India-EU relations, consider the following statements:
1. The EU is India's 22nd FTA partner.
2. The India-EU Security and Defence Partnership is the EU's third such partnership in Asia.
3. Japan and South Korea are the two Asian partners preceding India in this regard.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
10.x: All three statements are correct. The EU is India's 22nd FTA partner, and India is the EU's third Security and Defence Partnership in Asia after Japan and South Korea.
10.tq: Check the numerical rank and the two-country sequence together.

10.s: Cameco's agreement to supply uranium to India during 2027-2035 was concluded in the context of which bilateral relationship?
10.x: The uranium supply agreement for 2027-2035 was associated with the India-Canada relationship.
10.tq: Use the commodity and time period to identify the correct bilateral partner.

2. It is also referred to as ‘Sudarshan Chakra’.
3. It has a range of 400 km.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
10.x: The S-400 Triumf is a Russian-origin air-defence system, is referred to as ‘Sudarshan Chakra’, and has a stated range of 400 km.
10.tq: Combine related platform, alias and numerical facts in a coded statement question.

10.s: The MQ-9B Sea Guardian is best described as which of the following?
10.x: The MQ-9B Sea Guardian is a High Altitude Long Endurance drone supplied by General Atomics of the United States.
10.tq: Use the platform-description pairing to distinguish similar defence systems.

10.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Iron Dome, an Israeli system, is the model for India's Mission Sudarshan Chakra.
2. Mission Sudarshan Chakra aims at a multi-layer defence shield by 2030.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
10.x: Statement 1 is correct: Iron Dome (Israel) is the model. Statement 2 is wrong: the multi-layer shield is targeted by 2035, not 2030. So 1 only.
10.tq: Sudarshan Chakra shield = 2035, modelled on Israel's Iron Dome.

10.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Six more P-8I maritime patrol aircraft received Acceptance of Necessity in February 2026.
2. The P-8I is associated with the United States.
3. The GE F414 engine is intended for the AMCA Mk-1.
4. The AMCA Mk-2 engine is to be co-developed with Safran.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
10.x: All four statements are correct. Six additional US-associated P-8I aircraft received AoN in February 2026; the GE F414 is for AMCA Mk-1, while the Mk-2 engine is to be co-developed with Safran.
10.tq: Use a four-statement question to test platform, supplier, quantity and variant relationships.

10.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: CQB carbines — Bharat Forge and PLR
Heavyweight torpedoes for Kalvari submarines — Italy (WASS)
Kalvari submarines — Israel and Rafael Advanced Defense Systems
10.x: Kalvari-class Scorpene submarines are based on French Naval Group technology and are built at MDL. The other three pairings are correct.
10.tq: Find the wrong supplier–platform pairing among closely related defence procurements.

10.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Kalvari-class submarines is correct?
o: They are entirely of Russian design and were built at Cochin Shipyard.
They comprise six P-75 submarines, with INS Vaghsheer being the last one delivered in 2025.
They comprise four submarines, with INS Vaghsheer delivered in 2024.
They comprise eight submarines, with INS Vaghsheer delivered in 2026.
10.x: The P-75 programme comprises six Kalvari-class Scorpene submarines. INS Vaghsheer was the last submarine and was delivered in 2025.
10.tq: Test the count, programme name and latest platform status together.

10.s: RELOS, signed between India and Russia in February 2025 and operationalised in June 2026, relates to:
10.x: RELOS is the India–Russia logistics pact, signed in February 2025 and operationalised in June 2026.
10.tq: Identify the function of a bilateral defence agreement from its acronym and timeline.

10.s: The UNICORN stealth naval mast represents the first India–Japan co-manufacturing agreement in the field of:
10.x: UNICORN is a stealth naval mast and marks the first India–Japan co-manufacturing agreement in this area.
10.tq: Link a named defence technology with its specific domain and partner country.

10.s: With reference to BrahMos, which country is its first export customer, and where is the new BrahMos-NG plant located?
10.x: The Philippines is the first export customer, and the new BrahMos-NG plant is in the Lucknow Defence Corridor. B is wrong on both; C has the wrong customer; D has the wrong plant site.
10.tq: BrahMos: Philippines first buyer; NG plant Lucknow.

10.s: The Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Project, including Sittwe port, is associated with:
10.x: The Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Project is located in Myanmar and includes the Sittwe port component.
10.tq: Identify the host country of an India-assisted overseas project.

10.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The India–Myanmar–Thailand Trilateral Highway is 1,360 km long.
2. It is associated with Myanmar and Thailand.
3. The project is intended to improve regional connectivity.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
10.x: The highway is 1,360 km long, connects India through Myanmar to Thailand, and is a regional connectivity project.
10.tq: Combine a numerical, geographic and functional feature in one coded question.

10.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
10.x: Mangdechhu is an India-assisted hydropower project in Bhutan, not Nepal. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
10.tq: Find the incorrect host-country pairing among neighbouring-country projects.

10.s: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes Punatsangchhu-I from Mangdechhu?
o: Punatsangchhu-I is 1,200 MW and work resumed in April 2026, whereas Mangdechhu is 720 MW and was commissioned in 2019.
Punatsangchhu-I is 720 MW and was commissioned in 2019, whereas Mangdechhu is 1,200 MW and resumed work in 2026.
Both projects are in Mauritius and were commissioned in 2025.
Both projects are in Maldives and have a capacity of 400 MW each.
10.x: Punatsangchhu-I in Bhutan has a capacity of 1,200 MW and resumed work in April 2026. Mangdechhu, also in Bhutan, has a capacity of 720 MW and was commissioned in 2019.
10.tq: Compare two similar projects by capacity, status and year rather than memorising one isolated figure.

10.s: Which of the following statements regarding India’s response to the 2026 West Asia crisis is correct?
o: India suspended all naval activity in the Indian Ocean.
India deployed Navy escort missions named Sankalp and Urja Suraksha.
India joined the US–Israel attacks on Iran.
India transferred the Chabahar terminal to the United States.
10.x: India deployed Navy escort missions named Sankalp and Urja Suraksha in response to the crisis and disruption around Hormuz.
10.tq: Apply the current-affairs fact to a crisis-response scenario.

10.s: The principal criticism of the GE F414 arrangement is that:
o: Safran has retained all technology for the AMCA Mk-1 engine.
The engine is entirely manufactured in Russia, preventing US participation.
The single-crystal blade process remains with the United States, preserving Indian dependence.
The arrangement excludes the AMCA programme altogether.
10.x: The criticism is that the single-crystal blade manufacturing process remains with the United States, limiting technology transfer and maintaining dependence.
10.tq: Identify the specific technological dependency behind a policy criticism.

10.s: Heavy reliance on Russian defence platforms has been criticised mainly because it:
o: Limits diversification of India’s defence suppliers
Eliminates the need for indigenous production
Prevents India from operating naval platforms
Makes all Indian systems exclusively French
10.x: Dependence on Russian platforms is criticised because it limits diversification of India’s defence procurement sources.
10.tq: Connect a defence-procurement pattern with its strategic implication.

10.s:
Which of the following events were associated with Visakhapatnam in February 2026?
1. MILAN 2026
2. IFR 2026
3. IONS Conclave
4. DOSTI-16
Which of the statements given above are correct?
10.x: MILAN 2026, IFR 2026 and the IONS Conclave were associated with Visakhapatnam in February 2026. DOSTI-16 is not part of this grouping.
10.tq: Separate events held at the same venue from a familiar but unrelated naval exercise.

10.s: Nipun, the second Diving Support Vessel delivered to the Indian Navy at Visakhapatnam in August 2026, was built by:
10.x: Nipun (DSRV mother ship) was built by Hindustan Shipyard Ltd, Visakhapatnam, an AP angle. The other shipyards are not linked to Nipun in the notes.
10.tq: Nipun = HSL, Visakhapatnam.

11.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the radar configuration of NISAR?
o: L-band supplied by NASA and S-band supplied by ISRO
S-band supplied by NASA and L-band supplied by ISRO
Both L-band and S-band supplied by NASA
Both L-band and S-band supplied by ISRO
11.x: NISAR carries dual radar: NASA provides the L-band system and ISRO provides the S-band system.
11.tq: Resolve the paired-band confusion by fixing one agency to each radar band.

11.s: Which set of phenomena is specifically covered by NISAR’s Earth-observation objectives?
o: Solar corona, lunar craters and exoplanets
Only cloud formation and cyclone naming
Navigation signals, broadband and satellite docking
11.x: NISAR observes glaciers, earthquakes, land subsidence and biomass, among other Earth-system features.
11.tq: Select the group of applications consistent with an Earth-observation radar mission.

11.s:
Consider the following statements about the Gaganyaan mission:
1. It is designed to carry a crew of three to a 400 km orbit for three days.
2. NASA will provide ground-tracking support for the mission.
3. The second Integrated Air Drop Test (IADT-02) was done ahead of the uncrewed G1 flight.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
11.x: Statement 1 is correct (3 crew, 400 km, 3 days). Statement 2 is wrong: ESA, not NASA, will give ground-tracking support. Statement 3 is correct: IADT-02 (10 Apr 2026) preceded the uncrewed G1 flight. So 1 and 3 only.
11.tq: Gaganyaan = 3-400-3; tracking help from ESA.

11.s:
Which of the following statements about NISAR is correct?
1. It was launched in July 2025 from Sriharikota.
2. It is described as the costliest Earth-observation satellite, costing $1.5 billion.
3. It was launched by the Japanese H3 rocket.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
11.x: NISAR was launched from Sriharikota in July 2025 and is described as a $1.5-billion Earth-observation satellite. The Japanese H3 rocket is associated with Chandrayaan-5/LUPEX, not NISAR.
11.tq: Separate mission date and cost from the deliberately swapped launch vehicle.

11.s:
Consider the following statements about Chandrayaan-5 / LUPEX:
1. It is a joint mission of ISRO and JAXA.
2. It aims to study water-ice at the lunar south pole.
3. It is to be launched on India's LVM3 rocket.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
11.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: LUPEX is to fly on Japan's H3 rocket (around 2028). So 1 and 2 only.
11.tq: LUPEX = ISRO + JAXA, south-pole ice, on Japan's H3.

11.s: Which mission is described as India's first Earth-imaging satellite in geosynchronous orbit?
11.x: EOS-05, formerly GISAT-1A, is described as India's first Earth-imaging satellite in geosynchronous orbit.
11.tq: Identify the first-in-country claim from the satellite's function and orbit.

11.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Vikram-1 ('Aagaman')?
o: ISRO's first reusable launch vehicle; India became the second country after the US
Skyroot Aerospace's rocket; India became the fourth country after the US, Russia and China
Built by Skyroot Aerospace, Hyderabad; India's first privately developed orbital rocket, making India the third country after the US and China
Built by ISRO's Satish Dhawan Space Centre; India's first rocket to launch from a private pad
11.x: C is correct: Vikram-1 (18 Jul 2026) is Skyroot Aerospace's (Hyderabad) first private orbital rocket, making India the 3rd country after the US and China. A and D wrongly credit ISRO; B gives the wrong rank.
11.tq: Vikram-1 = Skyroot, Hyderabad; India 3rd after US and China.

11.s: TRISHNA is a thermal-infrared satellite mission being jointly developed by which agencies?
o: ESA and China National Space Administration
11.x: TRISHNA is an ISRO-CNES thermal-infrared satellite mission planned for launch on a PSLV.
11.tq: Identify the agency pair from the mission's technical objective.

11.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: OSIRIS-REx — renamed mission heading for asteroid Apophis
Aditya-L1 — observes the Sun from the L1 point
OSIRIS-APEX — returned Bennu samples to Earth in 2023
Artemis II — India's first Indian space station mission
11.x: Aditya-L1 observes the Sun from the L1 point. OSIRIS-REx returned Bennu samples in 2023, while its renamed continuation, OSIRIS-APEX, is heading toward Apophis.
11.tq: Separate the original mission from its renamed continuation and avoid reversed objectives.

11.s: Who was the first Indian to travel to the International Space Station?
11.x: Shubhanshu Shukla was the first Indian to travel to the ISS, during the Axiom-4 mission from 25 June to 15 July 2025.
11.tq: Distinguish the ISS milestone from earlier Indian space-flight associations.

11.s: India's stated space roadmap includes establishing its own space station by which year and sending an Indian to the Moon by which year?
11.x: The stated targets are an Indian space station by 2035 and an Indian on the Moon by 2040.
11.tq: Preserve the correct sequence of the two future milestones.

11.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the mission and its launch vehicle?
11.x: NISAR was launched on GSLV-F16. EOS-N1 used PSLV-C62, BlueBird Block-2 used LVM3-M6, and CMS-03 used LVM3.
11.tq: Start from the mission–vehicle pair and eliminate cross-swapped launchers.

11.s: BlueBird Block-2 was significant for carrying which payload from Indian soil?
11.x: BlueBird Block-2 carried a 6,100-kilogram payload, described as the heaviest payload launched from Indian soil. It was built by the US firm AST SpaceMobile.
11.tq: Distinguish the payload record from the different CMS-03 satellite mass.

11.s: Which statement correctly describes EOS-N1?
o: It was launched on PSLV-C62 on 12 January 2026 and failed.
It was launched on GSLV-F16 on 30 July 2025 and succeeded.
It was launched on LVM3-M6 on 24 December 2025 and carried BlueBird Block-2.
It was launched on H3 in 2028 for lunar ice exploration.
11.x: EOS-N1 was launched on PSLV-C62 on 12 January 2026 and the mission failed. The failure followed the earlier PSLV-C61/EOS-09 failure in May 2025.
11.tq: Check the mission date, vehicle and outcome together to defeat swapped entries.

11.s: Mission Drishti of GalaxEye is associated with which of the following?
o: India’s first domestic memory-chip packaging plant
The first private Indian 800 kN methane engine
The world’s first OptoSAR satellite launched on Falcon 9
The first private launch from the Dhanush pad using a 3D-printed engine
11.x: Mission Drishti, developed by GalaxEye, is associated with the world’s first OptoSAR satellite, launched on Falcon 9.
11.tq: Distinguish the mission by its payload and launch vehicle.

11.s: Proba-3 is associated with which objective?
o: Thermal infrared imaging of terrestrial natural resources
Two-spacecraft formation flying to study the Sun’s corona
11.x: ESA’s Proba-3 uses two-spacecraft formation flying to study the Sun’s corona.
11.tq: Match the agency mission with its distinctive two-spacecraft objective.

11.s: NASA invited ISRO to join which programme under the Artemis Accords?
11.x: NASA invited ISRO to join its lunar Moon Base programme under the Artemis Accords.
11.tq: Match the international invitation with its specific programme.

11.s: The ESA-China SMILE mission was launched on which vehicle from French Guiana?
11.x: The ESA-China SMILE mission was launched on a Vega-C rocket from French Guiana in May 2026.
11.tq: Match the international mission with its vehicle and launch location.

11.s: OSIRIS-APEX, in the news, is the renamed continuation of OSIRIS-REx. Which asteroid is it now heading for?
11.x: OSIRIS-APEX is heading for asteroid Apophis. Bennu is the asteroid from which OSIRIS-REx returned samples in 2023. 2024 YR4 is a separate asteroid in the news. Didymos is not mentioned in the notes for this mission.
11.tq: REx brought back Bennu; APEX goes to Apophis.

11.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its classification and associated organisation?
o: Agni-4 — Nuclear-capable MRBM — DRDO and Strategic Forces Command
Pralay — Subsonic cruise missile — Indian Air Force
BrahMos — Indigenous glide weapon — DRDO alone
Kusha — Air-to-surface anti-radiation missile — RCI Hyderabad
11.x: Agni-4 is a nuclear-capable medium-range ballistic missile associated with DRDO and the Strategic Forces Command. Pralay is a quasi-ballistic surface-to-surface missile, BrahMos is an India-Russia joint venture, and Kusha is a long-range surface-to-air missile.
11.tq: Use the developer-and-type pairing to eliminate swapped platform identities.

11.s: Kusha, which underwent its maiden test in July 2026, is best described as a:
o: Subsonic land-attack cruise missile developed by GTRE
Long-range glide bomb developed by JSR Dynamics and BEL
Long-range surface-to-air missile developed by DRDO
Air-to-surface anti-radiation missile developed by RCI Hyderabad
11.x: Kusha is a DRDO-developed long-range surface-to-air missile. It is described as India’s answer to, or rival of, systems such as the S-400 and Patriot.
11.tq: Match the weapon’s role with its developer rather than relying on a familiar missile name.

11.s:
Consider the following statements regarding LRLACM:
1. It is a subsonic land-attack cruise missile.
2. It has a range of more than 1,000 km.
3. It uses the Manik engine.
4. It is described as a successor to Nirbhay.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
11.x: All four statements are correct. LRLACM is a DRDO subsonic land-attack cruise missile with a range exceeding 1,000 km, uses the Manik engine and is described as Nirbhay’s successor.
11.tq: Check each technical specification separately before selecting the complete combination.

11.s: Which of the following is the first indigenous glide weapon mentioned in the context of the 2026 defence developments?
11.x: TARA is described as the first indigenous glide weapon, developed through DRDO and the IAF, and it underwent its maiden trial.
11.tq: Distinguish similarly grouped missile, glide-weapon and air-to-air weapon names.
